chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Adhere to the sweet pomegranate and eat it, for there is no seed that falls into the stomach of a believer except that it annihilates an illness and extinguishes the Satan of whispering from him.'

key_terms.شَيْطَانُ الْوَسْوَسَةِ: Satan of whispering (specifically referring to the whisperer/Satan associated with doubts and temptations)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of eating sweet pomegranates according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual and physical benefits of sweet pomegranates, noting that each seed consumed by a believer eliminates a specific illness and quenches the whispers of Satan. This recommendation underscores the Shia tradition of viewing food as both a means of physical healing and a tool for spiritual purification, linking bodily health with the mitigation of waswasa (divine whispers). The emphasis on 'sweet' pomegranates may also reflect the preference for foods that are gentle on the body and conducive to a calm, receptive state for worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is upon you with (eating) the sweet Pomegranate for there is none from a seed which falls in a stomach of a Believer except that it annihilates an illness and extinguishes the whispering of the Satan<sup>la</sup> from him’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘You must eat sweet pomegranate. Every grain that reaches the stomach of a believing person; it abolishes the illnesses and extinguishes the temptation of Satan thereof.’”
